findings.description: The generator is materialised inside the per-document test lambda, so each evaluation calls list() again on the same generator. The first evaluation uses it up and every later document tests against an empty list. The issue is not fixed and the result is now worse: the issue example returns only one document instead of two (and instead of the expected three).
findings.evidence: Probe /home/runner/work/_temp/autose/review-scratch/probe_one_of.py: `issue scenario: [{'tag': 'a'}]`, `first call 'a': True`, `second call 'a': False`.
findings.suggested_fix: Materialise once when the query is built, e.g. `items = list(items)` (or tuple) at the top of one_of(), before building the lambda and the hash. Then use `lambda value: value in items` and `freeze(items)`.

findings.description: The hash/equality tuple freezes the raw generator object. freeze() leaves generators unchanged, so the hash is identity-based rather than value-based, and equal queries built from equal generators compare unequal. Once the values are materialised before this line, freeze() turns them into a value-based tuple.
findings.evidence: utils.py:150-169 handles only dict/list/tuple/set. Probe: `equal generator queries compare equal: False`.
findings.suggested_fix: Freeze the materialised list instead of the generator.

findings.description: The new test evaluates the generator query only once, so it cannot catch the reported bug (failure on later documents). It passes against the broken implementation.
findings.evidence: The full suite passes (230 passed) while the probe shows the issue scenario still fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that runs the issue example through db.search on MemoryStorage with several matching documents and asserts all three results, and/or evaluates the same query several times.
